items.stem:
A part of an R program is given below:
> x <- 3
> f = function(y) {
  x <- 5
  x + y
}
> f(4)
The output of the program is:
items.explanation: Idea: assignment inside an R function creates a local variable, which shadows the global one for that call only. Option 7 is what you would get by wrongly using the global x = 3. Working: Inside f, x <- 5 creates a local x that masks the global x = 3, so f(4) returns 5 + 4 = 9. Official answer: B (9).
